ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal dashed lines, points P and Q are on the lower dashed line, and points R and S are on the upper dashed line; PQ and RS are parallel horizontal diameters. The left semicircle has PQ as its diameter and opens upward, and the right semicircle has RS as its diameter and opens downward; the two semicircular arcs are tangent in the middle; line segment PS connects from the lower-left P to the upper-right S. In the figure, the upper dashed line is tangent to the top of the left semicircle, and the lower dashed line is tangent to the bottom of the right semicircle, so the horizontal lines on which the two diameters lie are separated by 1 radius length. Reasoning: The radius of each semicircle is 1, so each diameter has length 2. Let P=(0,0), Q=(2,0), then the center of the left circle C=(1,0). The diameter RS of the right semicircle is on the upper horizontal line, and its center D is on the line y=1. Let D=(1+h,1), so S=(2+h,1). The two circles with radius 1 are externally tangent, so the center distance CD=2. Thus h^2+1^2=2^2, obtaining h^2=3, taking the positive value h=√3. Therefore the horizontal displacement of PS is 2+√3, and the vertical displacement is 1, so PS^2=(2+√3)^2+1=8+4√3.
